To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the molecular events that occur during progression of human colonic adenocarcinomas to a metastatic phenotype include the acquisition of sensitivity to apoptotic stimuli.
the levels of staurospore-induced apoptosis are significantly increased in metastatic colon adenomas, and that these cells have significantly lower levels of the anti-apoptotic protein Bcl-2.
metastatic colon cancer cells are more susceptible than primary colon cancer cells to apoptosis and that metastatic colon cancers have increased apoptosis compared with primary tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular events that are responsible for the acquisition of the metastastic phenotype.
identifying and characterizing molecular alterations that occur during the progression from normal colon mucosa to metastatic colon cancer.
identifying and characterizing the genetic changes that are associated with the acquisition of the metastasizing phenotype.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
apoptosis is a key event in the progression and metastasis of colon cancer.
the molecular events that occur during the acquisition of the metastasizing phenotype may sensitize tumor cells to some proapoptotic stimuli.

the molecular events leading to metastatic progression may sensitize colon cancer to apoptosis, and that the increased apoptosis observed in colon metastases may be due, at least in part, to decreased Bcl-2 expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
apoptosis may be an important mechanism of cell death during the metastatic process.
increased apoptosis in metastatic tumors may be an important factor in the selection of metastatic variants.
the molecular events that lead to the development of the metastatic potential in human colon cancer cells also sensitize them to apoptosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular changes associated with metastasis may render cells more susceptible to apoptotic stimuli.
apoptosis can be a mechanism by which metastatic cancer cells are eliminated from the body.

the metastatic phenotype is associated with increased sensitivity of tumor cells to apoptosis, suggesting that the metastatic tumor may be more sensitive to some forms of therapy than its nonmetastatic counterpart.
